title: Guava: Distilling Frontier VLMs into a Compact Agent through a Robotic Manipulation Harness

title: Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots
summary: An embodied harness of discrete incremental semantic action units, grounded deterministically by embodiment-specific interpreters (Franka, Piper, ManiSkill, Isaac Lab, LIBERO). Frontier VLMs (Gemini default) drive it zero-shot with plugins for planning, memory and recovery. GUMI lets humans or GUI/computer-use agents 'play' the robot in a browser to record (obs, action) pairs, which fine-tune small VLMs (Qwen3.5 0.8B-9B, Gemma4) that emit one action token per step, planner-free.
agent_component: Zero-shot: frontier VLM with a plugin harness. Data collection: humans or GUI-driving agents (computer-use agent / GPT web operator) via GUMI. Fine-tuned: small VLM.
embodied_component: Deterministic embodiment interpreters for semantic action units (impedance control on Franka, joint streaming on Piper; sim interpreters)
scope_note: Zero-shot mode: external-frontier. Fine-tuned mode: small VLM emitting one semantic action token per step, with no planner or reasoning, so effectively a VLA over a semantic action space. Its training data comes from human/agent GUI demos, not frontier-agent reasoning traces. The deployed small model is weakly agentic (closed-loop, no deliberation). Likely the user's 'show harness'. Repo also announces a competing awesome-list survey (Awesome-Multimodal-Embodied-Agent).

summary: Keeps the foundation model frozen and evolves the surrounding system (context management, persistent memory, hierarchical skills) through validated, execution-driven system edits; includes physical-robot evaluation.
agent_component: Frozen FM agent plus an editing/evolution agent
embodied_component: Robot executing skills (sim and physical)
scope_note: Names the key 2026 idea, 'system-as-policy': the learnable object is the harness, not the weights.
families: Memory, lifelong learning and self-evolving embodied agents (2023-2026)

title: RoboRSI: Stable, Efficient, and Reusable Robot Self-Evolution in Complex Real-World Environments
summary: A multi-agent harness (Manager, Planner, Engineer, Reviewer) refines a task-skill tree from execution traces, consolidates stable workflows into code, can train learned policies from the execution data, and gates skill changes with regression checks; LIBERO variants plus real robot.
agent_component: Multi-agent LLM team (manager, planner, engineer, reviewer)
embodied_component: Skills and learned policies on a real robot and LIBERO
scope_note: A research blog and open-source harness with no arXiv paper. It moves skills along a ladder from exploration to code to learned policy.
families: Memory, lifelong learning and self-evolving embodied agents (2023-2026)

title: Self-Evolving Embodied Agents via Skill-Harness Evolution
summary: Keeps the model frozen and jointly optimizes skills and the harness to make embodied agents self-evolving.
agent_component: Frozen FM agent plus a skill/harness optimizer
embodied_component: Embodied skill executor (details unverified)
scope_note: Only a one-line description was verified. It belongs to the frozen-model, evolving-harness group.
families: Memory, lifelong learning and self-evolving embodied agents (2023-2026)

title: Skill2Real: Agentic Skill Learning for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Robot Manipulation
summary: An agent learns hierarchical executable skills through a shared robot API in simulation, using diagnosis and validation gates, then transfers the frozen skill memory to a physical UR5e without target-task policy fine-tuning.
agent_component: LLM/coding agent with simulation diagnosis
embodied_component: UR5e manipulator executing skill code through the robot API
scope_note: Skill memory learned in simulation and frozen for deployment: lifelong learning split into a practice phase and a deployment phase.
families: Memory, lifelong learning and self-evolving embodied agents (2023-2026)

title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
summary: Improves a persistent skill library and system prompt through practice in reconstructed simulation, diagnosis of failures with privileged information, and cross-task validation, then freezes the calibrated system for physical deployment.
agent_component: Foundation-model agent plus a privileged diagnosis process
embodied_component: Physical robot executing library skills
scope_note: Self-evolution happens before deployment in a reconstructed simulation, which places it between the memory family and the environment-builder family.
families: Memory, lifelong learning and self-evolving embodied agents (2023-2026)

title: RoboBridge: A Self-Evolving Embodied Agent Framework for Sim-to-Real Transfer
summary: Transfers revisable procedural skills from simulation to physical tasks and validates further skill updates from execution feedback, treating a frozen VLA as a tool with optional inference-time guidance.
agent_component: Foundation-model agent with a revisable procedural-skill memory
embodied_component: Frozen VLA plus skills on a physical robot
scope_note: Self-evolving skills wrapped around a frozen VLA used as a tool.
families: Memory, lifelong learning and self-evolving embodied agents (2023-2026)

title: Learning Without Losing Identity: Capability Evolution for Embodied Agents
summary: Keeps a fixed high-level planner and puts all learning into versioned skill modules that are trained, promoted through a held-out gate, rolled back on regression, and run behind a runtime governance layer; companion paper Governed Capability Evolution is arXiv 2604.08059.
agent_component: Fixed LLM planner plus a governance layer
embodied_component: Versioned learned skill modules on robot tasks
scope_note: Belongs to the governance-of-lifelong-evolution sub-line. The agent does not decide updates itself (a gate process does), so it is a systems-engineering boundary case.
families: Memory, lifelong learning and self-evolving embodied agents (2023-2026)

title: GSMem: 3D Gaussian Splatting as Persistent Spatial Memory for Zero-Shot Embodied Exploration and Reasoning
summary: Judging from the title, it uses 3D Gaussian Splatting as a persistent spatial memory that an embodied agent queries for zero-shot exploration and reasoning.
agent_component: VLM agent querying the 3DGS memory (details unverified)
embodied_component: Exploring embodied agent / mobile robot
scope_note: A spatial-memory representation paper; the agentic loop is unverified. Mimir (2608.04933), eMEM (2606.03374) and SnapMem/3D-Mem belong to the same representation group and are in scope only when an agent reads and writes the memory to act.
families: Memory, lifelong learning and self-evolving embodied agents (2023-2026)

title: Self-evolving Embodied AI (survey)
summary: A survey by Feng, Wang and Zhu on embodied AI systems that evolve themselves.
agent_component: n/a (survey)
embodied_component: n/a
scope_note: Not a primary paper. A competing survey to differentiate from: our framing must make agency (a foundation-model agent closing the loop) the criterion, not self-evolution as such.
families: Memory, lifelong learning and self-evolving embodied agents (2023-2026)

title: NavGPT: Explicit Reasoning in Vision-and-Language Navigation with Large Language Models
summary: A purely LLM-based instruction-following VLN agent: visual foundation models turn each viewpoint into text, and GPT-4 reasons explicitly over the instruction, observations and history to pick the next navigable viewpoint.
agent_component: GPT-4 / GPT-3.5, zero-shot, step-wise ReAct-style reasoning-then-act loop over textualised observations
embodied_component: Discrete nav-graph agent in Matterport3D (R2R): it teleports between viewpoints and has no low-level control
scope_note: The canonical case where the agent IS the navigation policy. The embodiment is thin, though: on a discrete graph the action space looks like web navigation, so this tests whether graph-VLN counts as embodied.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: Discuss Before Moving: Visual Language Navigation via Multi-expert Discussions
summary: Before each move, a navigator agent consults several LLM/VLM 'domain experts' (instruction analysis, perception, completion estimation, decision testing) and acts on their consensus.
agent_component: Several prompted LLM/VLM role-agents plus a navigator LLM, zero-shot
embodied_component: Discrete R2R nav-graph navigation in simulation
scope_note: Here 'multi-agent' means several roles inside one decision loop for one body, not several robots. The multi-agent label should keep these two cases apart.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: MapGPT: Map-Guided Prompting with Adaptive Path Planning for Vision-and-Language Navigation
summary: A GPT-4V agent keeps an online topological map, turns it into a prompt, and does adaptive multi-step path planning for zero-shot VLN.
agent_component: GPT-4V, zero-shot, map-in-context reasoning and planning loop
embodied_component: Discrete R2R nav-graph navigation (simulation)
role: controller and planner with explicit map memory
scope_note: Shows memory and representation (the map) as a harness component outside the model. Same thin-embodiment caveat as NavGPT.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: InstructNav: Zero-shot System for Generic Instruction Navigation in Unexplored Environment
summary: A training-free system for generic instruction navigation (ObjNav, VLN, demand-driven): an LLM plans a Dynamic Chain-of-Navigation that multi-sourced value maps turn into executable trajectories, with no pre-built map.
agent_component: GPT-4-class LLM/VLM that repeatedly re-plans the Dynamic Chain-of-Navigation
embodied_component: Value-map-guided local planner in continuous Habitat environments
role: planner / subgoal generator that closes the loop through value maps
scope_note: The LLM owns the high-level control flow (what to seek next, when to replan). The geometric executor is classical.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: SG-Nav: Online 3D Scene Graph Prompting for LLM-based Zero-shot Object Navigation
summary: Builds an online hierarchical 3D scene graph, prompts an LLM with hierarchical chain-of-thought to score frontiers by how likely the goal is nearby, and re-perceives the scene to correct false detections.
agent_component: LLM queried at each frontier decision on a scene-graph prompt
embodied_component: Frontier-based exploration with a point-goal local planner (Habitat; real-robot demos)
role: heuristic scorer inside a fixed exploration loop
scope_note: The LLM acts as a scoring function. The hand-written frontier loop owns control flow (when to call, when to stop). This is the 'LLM-as-module vs LLM-as-agent' boundary.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: UniGoal: Towards Universal Zero-shot Goal-oriented Navigation
summary: Puts object, image and text goals into one uniform graph and uses LLM-based scene-graph/goal-graph matching to drive a staged exploration policy (expand, infer, verify).
agent_component: LLM reasoning over scene and goal graphs at stage transitions
embodied_component: Classical mapping and local planning in continuous simulation
scope_note: The staged pipeline is still hand-designed. The LLM makes more decisions than in SG-Nav but does not own the loop.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: VLFM: Vision-Language Frontier Maps for Zero-Shot Semantic Navigation
summary: A pre-trained vision-language model scores RGB observations against the target text to build a value map over occupancy-map frontiers, and the robot explores the highest-value frontier; it was deployed on Spot.
agent_component: none (the VLM is used only as a per-frame value function)
embodied_component: Frontier exploration with a point-goal policy on a real Spot and in Habitat
scope_note: Negative boundary. A foundation model used as a stateless scorer, with no reasoning loop, tool choice or termination decision, is not an agent.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: Mobility VLA: Multimodal Instruction Navigation with Long-Context VLMs and Topological Graphs
summary: A long-context VLM (Gemini 1.5 Pro) reads a demonstration tour video plus a multimodal instruction to find the goal frame, and a topological-graph low-level policy then navigates there.
agent_component: Frontier long-context VLM, called once per instruction to ground the goal
embodied_component: Topological-graph navigation policy on a real mobile robot
scope_note: Hierarchical, but the VLM makes one shot per query with no iterative feedback. Weak agency despite the 'VLA' name. Naming does not decide scope.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: NavCoT: Boosting LLM-Based Vision-and-Language Navigation via Learning Disentangled Reasoning
summary: Fine-tunes an open LLM to produce a structured reasoning chain (imagine the next view, filter candidates, predict the action) before each VLN action, internalising NavGPT-style reasoning.
agent_component: Fine-tuned open LLM that reasons in-weights; no external tools
embodied_component: Discrete VLN action selection in simulation
scope_note: The navigation analogue of ECoT. Reasoning is internalised but there is no harness or tool use. Under a 'loop + tools' definition it sits at the edge.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: AgenticNav: Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation as a Tool-Calling Harness
summary: Recasts zero-shot VLN as tool calling: a VLM agent gets pixel-target actions, on-demand depth queries and selective visual-memory recall as tools. Evaluated in VLN-CE and on two physical robots.
agent_component: Frontier VLM (GPT-5.5 per NavHarness's baseline table), multi-turn tool-calling loop
embodied_component: Pixel-goal / waypoint executor on continuous-environment simulation and two real robots
scope_note: Clear core case. The contribution is the harness (action tools, perception-on-demand, memory) and not the model.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: NavHarness: Adaptive Goals for Agentic Vision-and-Language Navigation
summary: Four agents (Goal, Visuomotor, Verify, Memory) split one VLN loop. Goals and completion questions are set adaptively, verification gates progress, and history is compressed at verified boundaries. Reports 79.0% SR on R2R-CE (+5.0 over a plain Codex CLI baseline) and 83.3% over 24 real-world trials.
agent_component: Frontier multimodal models (Qwen-3.6-plus, GPT-5.6-Sol, GPT-6-Astra), decomposed into role agents
embodied_component: Monocular forward/turn/stop navigation in VLN-CE and on a real robot
role: controller plus internal verifier and memory manager
scope_note: Core. The page shows an unmodified coding agent (Codex CLI + GPT-6-Astra) reaching 74% SR zero-shot on R2R-CE: a general agent with a thin harness is already a competitive low-level navigation policy. The role agents here are a harness-internal split, not embodied multi-agent.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: ASENA: Self-evolving Agents for Embodied Navigation
summary: A general-purpose coding agent navigates through sensor and execution tools and keeps persistent notes and programs, improving on repeated tasks in simulation and in supervised humanoid demonstrations.
agent_component: General-purpose coding agent (CLI-style), self-evolving through notes and programs
embodied_component: Navigation execution tools on simulated robots and a humanoid
role: controller + self-programmer (writes and reuses its own navigation programs)
scope_note: Mixes runtime control with self-modification of the harness (programs/skills) across episodes. It shows that 'timing' is about which loop is closed, not runtime vs offline. Details come from list annotations only.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: ReMEmbR: Building and Reasoning Over Long-Horizon Spatio-Temporal Memory for Robots
summary: VILA captions of long robot deployments are stored in a vector database. An LLM agent iteratively queries it with text, position and time retrieval tools to answer questions and output navigation goals.
agent_component: LLM agent with retrieval tools in a multi-step query loop
embodied_component: Mobile robot navigation stack (goal-pose execution)
scope_note: Memory-as-tool for an embodied agent (NVIDIA). The agent's physical output is only a goal pose; the low level is classical.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: Language-Grounded Dynamic Scene Graphs for Interactive Object Search with Mobile Manipulation
summary: An LLM reasons over a dynamically updated room/object scene graph and its action history, issuing high-level actions (navigate, open, explore, done) for interactive object search with a mobile manipulator.
agent_component: LLM in a closed loop choosing high-level actions from structured scene-graph state
embodied_component: Mobile manipulator skills (navigation, door/drawer opening) in simulation and the real world
scope_note: A classic 'agent orchestrates skills' case for mobile manipulation.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: CheckVLA: Execution-Time Verification with Action-Conditioned World Model for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation
summary: Verifies a VLA's long-horizon mobile-manipulation execution at run time by checking outcomes against an action-conditioned world model's predictions.
agent_component: Unclear / likely none (the verifier is a world model, not a reasoning agent); only the title was verified
embodied_component: VLA-driven mobile manipulator
scope_note: Fills the monitor role that Code-as-Monitor fills, but possibly without an agent. This shows the definition must be about who fills a role (an agent that owns control flow) and not about the role alone.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: Trinity: A Modular Humanoid Robot AI System
summary: A modular humanoid system that combines RL-based whole-body/locomotion control with VLM perception and LLM task planning.
agent_component: LLM task planner + VLM perception (details from memory)
embodied_component: Humanoid with an RL whole-body controller
scope_note: A system-integration paper. How deep the agentic loop goes (replanning, feedback) could not be verified.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: KPI: A Promptable Kernel for Physical Interaction on Humanoids
summary: A promptable contact kernel sits between the trajectory source and an unmodified whole-body tracker. From one instruction, a vision-language agent writes both the reference motion and an 'interaction contract' (direction, requirement, force range), and KPI adapts stiffness, damping and feedforward at contact rate. Demonstrated on winch operation, door opening and box transport.
agent_component: Vision-language agent that writes motion and contract specifications without task-specific code
embodied_component: Humanoid whole-body tracker plus the KPI contact-adaptation kernel
role: programmer / commander that writes a typed interface to a learned controller
scope_note: Shows the 'action interface' axis: the agent emits a contract-level program, between skill calls and raw actions.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: InterEvolve: Test-Time Evolution of Reward Programs for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
summary: An LLM evolves staged reward programs from simulation feedback and a verified skill library, while numerical search tunes constants for a fixed pretrained humanoid controller. Deployed on a physical Unitree G1.
agent_component: LLM in an evolutionary reward-program search loop with simulation feedback
embodied_component: Pretrained humanoid whole-body controller, tuned in simulation and deployed on a real G1
scope_note: Eureka-line: the agent shapes the training signal and is absent at run time. In scope only if the definition admits agents whose output is an artifact (reward, code, data) that the embodied system later runs. That is also the test case for ENPIRE-style development agents.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: AllDayNav: Lifelong Navigation via Real-World Reinforcement Learning
summary: A self-evolving multimodal memory, with VLM-written keyframe descriptions, drives self-instruction: a VLM generates tasks and retrieves visual goals from memory, and CQL-based offline RL keeps refining a VLA navigation policy on a real Go2 without human supervision.
agent_component: VLM used for memory captioning, self-instruction and goal retrieval (backbone not verified)
embodied_component: VLA waypoint-prediction navigation policy trained with real-world RL on a Unitree Go2
role: teacher / curriculum and data engine for policy RL
scope_note: The 'agent' mostly generates tasks and retrieves goals for an RL learner, which is weak agency. It tests whether a self-instructing curriculum generator counts, and lines up with the data-engine role.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: LOVON: Legged Open-Vocabulary Object Navigator
summary: Combines LLM hierarchical task planning with open-vocabulary detection and a language-to-motion model, so legged robots (quadrupeds and a humanoid) can do long-range open-world object navigation.
agent_component: LLM task decomposer/planner (backbone not verified; details from memory)
embodied_component: Legged locomotion controllers on quadruped and humanoid platforms
scope_note: The LLM decomposes long missions, but how much feedback-driven replanning happens is unclear. It sits between 'LLM planner' and 'agent'.
families: Agentic navigation, mobile manipulation and humanoid agents (2023-2026)

title: Gen2Sim: Scaling up Robot Learning in Simulation with Generative Models
summary: Turns images into 3D assets with generative models, uses an LLM to label physical properties and write task descriptions and reward functions, and trains RL policies in simulation.
agent_component: LLM queried in a mostly single pass for asset physics, tasks and reward code
embodied_component: RL manipulation policies in simulation (articulated-object skills)
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Borderline: mostly feed-forward generation, with little loop from policy or execution feedback back to the LLM.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: Holodeck: Language Guided Generation of 3D Embodied AI Environments
summary: GPT-4 turns a text prompt into a 3D house (floor plan, materials, Objaverse object retrieval and spatial-relation constraints solved by an optimiser). The generated scenes are used to train object-navigation agents for new scene types.
agent_component: LLM program (GPT-4) emitting layout specifications and constraints, with a constraint solver
embodied_component: ObjectNav embodied agents trained in AI2-THOR
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Borderline: single-pass generation with no feedback from policy learning; navigation rather than manipulation.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: RoboCasa: Large-Scale Simulation of Everyday Tasks for Generalist Robots (and RoboCasa365, ICLR 2026)
summary: A large kitchen simulation framework with AI-generated assets and composite tasks (365 tasks in RoboCasa365) made with LLM guidance. It is used to scale imitation data and benchmark generalist policies.
agent_component: LLM used as an authoring aid for task creation; text-to-3D/image generators for assets
embodied_component: Generalist imitation policies and VLAs trained and benchmarked in RoboCasa
scope_note: Train-time only: YES (also used for evaluation). Borderline: the LLM supports human task design rather than running a closed loop.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: GenManip: LLM-driven Simulation for Generalizable Instruction-Following Manipulation
summary: An LLM-driven tabletop simulation platform that builds task-oriented scene graphs and instructions to generate diverse manipulation tasks for evaluating and training generalisable policies.
agent_component: LLM generating task-oriented scene graphs and instructions
embodied_component: Instruction-following manipulation policies (modular and end-to-end) evaluated and trained in simulation
scope_note: Train-time only: YES (mainly an evaluation benchmark). Borderline: generative authoring with weak closed-loop agency.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: EmbodiedGen V2: An Agentic, Simulation-Ready 3D World Engine for Embodied AI
summary: An agent-driven engine (GPT or Codex backend, also a Claude Code plugin) that turns language, images and edit commands into physically plausible, simulation-ready assets, scenes and task-driven interactive worlds. A companion study (2603.18532) trains VLAs with RL only in generated worlds, raising success from 9.7% to 79.8% in sim and 21.7% to 75.0% on a real robot.
agent_component: General coding agent (GPT agent or Codex CLI) driving generation tools and scene-graph composition
embodied_component: VLA policies trained with sim RL in generated worlds and deployed on real robots
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Core 2026 case: a generic coding agent with a domain harness builds training worlds, which brings the env-builder and developer families together.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: SceneWeaver: All-in-One 3D Scene Synthesis with an Extensible and Self-Reflective Agent
summary: An LLM agent plans over an extensible set of scene-synthesis tools in a reason-act-reflect loop to build realistic, physically plausible and interactable 3D scenes for embodied AI.
agent_component: LLM planner with tool library and self-reflection
embodied_component: Interactive 3D scenes meant for embodied simulation; no policy trained in the core paper
scope_note: Train-time only: YES (scene asset). Borderline: strongly agentic, but its output is not coupled to policy learning in the paper. It is in scope only if the survey counts environment authoring with no policy downstream.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: OMNI-EPIC: Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness with Environments Programmed in Code
summary: Foundation models write both simulated environments and reward/success-detection code as programs. A model of interestingness filters tasks against an archive, giving an open-ended curriculum for an RL agent.
agent_component: LLM environment and reward code generator plus an interestingness/success judge, looping over an archive
embodied_component: RL agent (simulated robot) trained on the generated task sequence in PyBullet
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Core: an open-ended loop where the agent authors tasks and rewards and gets learner-progress feedback.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: REvolve: Reward Evolution with Large Language Models using Human Feedback
summary: LLM-driven evolutionary search over reward-function code, with human preference feedback as the fitness signal, for autonomous driving, humanoid locomotion and dexterous manipulation.
agent_component: LLM as mutation/crossover operator over reward programs, with human fitness
embodied_component: RL policies (driving, humanoid, dexterous hand) in simulation
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Core (Eureka-like loop), with a human as verifier.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: Guiding Pretraining in Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models
summary: An LLM suggests goals from a text description of the current state, and the agent gets intrinsic reward for transitions semantically similar to those goals. Evaluated in Crafter and the Housekeep household simulator.
agent_component: LLM goal proposer queried at each step
embodied_component: RL agent in Crafter / Housekeep (simulated embodiment)
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Borderline: the LLM is a goal oracle (no tool use or self-revision), and the embodiment is game-like.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: OMNI: Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness
summary: A foundation-model 'model of interestingness' picks tasks that are both learnable and interesting from a large task space, forming an auto-curriculum for an RL agent in Crafter and BabyAI.
agent_component: LLM interestingness judge over a task archive
embodied_component: RL agent in grid/game embodied environments
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Borderline: the LLM acts as a judge rather than an author, and the embodiment is not robotic. It is the precursor of OMNI-EPIC.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: RL-VLM-F: Reinforcement Learning from Vision Language Foundation Model Feedback
summary: A frontier VLM gives preference labels over pairs of observation images for a text goal. A reward model learned from these labels drives RL for manipulation and deformable-object tasks.
agent_component: Frontier VLM as a pairwise preference judge (no tool use or iteration)
embodied_component: RL manipulation policies in simulation
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Borderline: foundation model as judge with no authoring and no closed loop. Better covered as the critic/verifier component of the anatomy.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: GRAPE: Generalizing Robot Policy via Preference Alignment
summary: Aligns a VLA with trajectory-wise preference optimisation. Preferences are ranked by costs built from VLM-proposed stage decompositions and keypoint spatiotemporal constraints, which allows customisable alignment goals such as safety or efficiency.
agent_component: VLM proposing stages and keypoint constraints (cost specification)
embodied_component: VLA (OpenVLA-class) fine-tuned by preference optimisation
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Borderline: the VLM writes a cost specification in one pass. It shows reward design moving to VLA post-training.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: A Generalist Pair-wise Progress Critic Model for Vision-Language-Action Robots
summary: A generalist pair-wise progress critic for VLA robots that scores relative task progress between observations to provide dense learning signals (VLAC follow-up).
agent_component: Learned VLM critic (non-agentic)
embodied_component: VLA policies improved with critic signals
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Out: a learned reward model with no agentic loop. Cover it in an anatomy 'critic' section. Details beyond the title come from the VLAC repo only.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: Robo-Dopamine: General Process Reward Modeling for High-Precision Robotic Manipulation
summary: A general process reward model (GRM) trained on a large progress-annotated corpus (35M-sample dataset) that provides step-wise dense rewards for RL of high-precision manipulation policies.
agent_component: Learned VLM process reward model (non-agentic)
embodied_component: Manipulation policies / VLAs trained with RL
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Out: a reward function, not an agent. It is the robotics counterpart of LLM process reward models.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: Robometer: Scaling General-Purpose Robotic Reward Models via Trajectory Comparisons
summary: Trains general-purpose robot reward models from trajectory comparisons on RBM-1M, so that failed and suboptimal trajectories can be used instead of only expert-demonstration progress labels.
agent_component: Learned reward foundation model (4B) (non-agentic)
embodied_component: Robot policies trained or evaluated with the learned reward
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Out: a reward model with no agentic loop.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: ReWiND: Language-Guided Rewards Teach Robot Policies without New Demonstrations
summary: Learns a language-conditioned reward model from a few demonstrations with video-rewinding augmentation, then uses it for offline RL pretraining and online RL on new tasks without new demonstrations.
agent_component: Learned video-language reward model (non-agentic)
embodied_component: RL manipulation policies (MetaWorld and real arm)
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Out: no agent.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: RoboCLIP: One Demonstration is Enough to Learn Robot Policies
summary: Uses a pretrained video-language model's similarity between a policy rollout and a single video or text demonstration as a sparse episode reward for RL.
agent_component: Pretrained video-language encoder (non-agentic)
embodied_component: RL manipulation policies in simulation
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Out: an embedding-similarity reward with no agency.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: Vision-Language Models are Zero-Shot Reward Models for Reinforcement Learning
summary: Uses CLIP image-text similarity as a zero-shot reward to train MuJoCo humanoid poses and classic-control tasks from language prompts.
agent_component: CLIP (non-agentic)
embodied_component: RL policies (MuJoCo humanoid)
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Out: a similarity reward. The arXiv ID was not seen in fetched sources, so it is left blank.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: World-Env: Leveraging World Model as a Virtual Environment for VLA Post-Training
summary: Uses a video world model as a virtual environment for RL post-training of VLAs (OpenVLA-OFT on LIBERO). A VLM-guided reflector supplies reward and episode termination; the reflector detail is from memory.
agent_component: Frozen VLM judge (reflector) inside a learned simulator
embodied_component: VLA (OpenVLA-OFT) post-trained with RL
role: reward/termination judge in a world-model environment
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Borderline: the closest example of agentic world-model-in-the-loop training, but the VLM only judges. A learned simulator alone is not an agent.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: VLA-RFT: Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Fine-tuning with Verified Rewards in World Simulators
summary: A world model trained on real interaction data acts as a controllable simulator for VLA reinforcement fine-tuning, with dense trajectory-level rewards computed against goal-achieving references.
agent_component: None (learned world simulator + reference-based reward)
embodied_component: VLA fine-tuned with RL in the world model
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Out: world-model RL with no agent. It is an explicit boundary exclusion and belongs to the World Action Model / world-model survey territory.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: WMPO: World Model-based Policy Optimization for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: On-policy GRPO for VLAs inside a pixel-space video world model, with imagined trajectories scored by a learned VideoMAE reward model and no real-environment interaction.
agent_component: None (world model + learned reward classifier)
embodied_component: VLA policies (sim and real)
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Out: non-agentic; included only to mark the boundary.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: DreamGen: Unlocking Generalization in Robot Learning through Video World Models
summary: Fine-tuned video world models generate synthetic robot videos for new behaviours and environments. Pseudo-actions are recovered and the resulting neural trajectories train visuomotor policies.
agent_component: None (generative video model + inverse dynamics/latent actions)
embodied_component: Visuomotor policies (GR00T-class) trained on synthetic trajectories
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Out: generative data without an agent. It is the generative-model counterpart of agentic data engines.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)

title: Learning Visual Parkour from Generated Images
summary: An LLM generates diverse text prompts for conditional image generators, while physics simulation provides geometry. A quadruped visual parkour policy is trained on-policy on the generated imagery and transferred to the real world.
agent_component: LLM prompt generator (single pass)
embodied_component: Quadruped visual locomotion/parkour policy, sim-to-real
scope_note: Train-time only: YES. Borderline: the LLM is a diversity generator, not an agent.
families: Agent as environment / task / reward / curriculum / data builder for embodied learning (agency acting on the learning problem rather than on the world)
